stack_detection.signature: single CANVAS element covering the viewport; DOM has no text/interactive nodes inside it

cells.channel_setup: Chromium via CDP; DOMSnapshot distilled view.

t1_read_text.detail: Score/level text is drawn INTO the canvas; structured view sees none of it. But it does not lie: it emits exactly '[pixels] canvas 0,0,1280,800' — the whole screen declared as one opaque region. Agent must fall back to vision on that rect.

t2_enumerate.detail: No enumerable elements — correctly reported as one opaque canvas, not a fabricated tree.

t4_living_screen.detail: A real game would animate; the structured channel would keep declaring the same opaque rect (no free change signal) — pixels/diffing of the crop is the only option.

t5_blind_action.detail: No coordinates derivable from structure; aiming requires vision on the crop.

t6_pictorial.detail: THE key safety result: the opaque region is DECLARED with its exact rect. Failure is explicit, not silent — a router can detect 'structure covers 0% of this screen' before acting and switch to the pixel path.

measurements.notes: This is the wanted NEGATIVE that proves the perimeter law and the safety property simultaneously: where structure yields nothing (games, video, remote desktop), it says so explicitly. Full-screen canvas apps (games, some Google Docs modes) collapse to the pixel baseline — no gain, but no silent loss either.

runtime_verification.method: compare structured view coverage to screenshot content
runtime_verification.agreement: structured view explicitly covers 0% of on-screen content and declares it (opaque rect) — consistent, not divergent

cells.app: GNOME Text Editor — hard-text stress (ligatures, accents, RTL Arabic, emoji, CJK)

stack_detection.signature: libgtk-4.so; text nodes name their font per run

cells.channel_setup: GSK render tree via gdb tap; per-text-node glyph IDs decoded with the node's OWN named font (reverse cmap) + Unicode NFKC + BiDi reorder.

t1_read_text.detail: All runs recovered when decoded with the correct per-node font (the tree names it, and font fallback splits runs by font): Latin 'office finance flag' ✓; precomposed accents 'café','naïve' ✓ (glyphs 171→é, 177→ï); CJK '你好' ✓ (WenQuanYi font); emoji '😀' ✓ (Noto Color Emoji, single color glyph 883). RTL Arabic recovered as presentation forms in visual order (ﺎﺒﺣﺮﻣ), then NFKC → base letters and reverse → 'مرحبا' exactly. Ligatures decompose via NFKC (ﬁ→fi, ﬂ→fl).

measurements.notes: Stronger than predicted. The 'glyph problem' is largely solved by three cheap steps: (1) use the per-run font the tree already names (fallback splits runs, so emoji/CJK land in their own nodes with the right font); (2) reverse cmap; (3) Unicode NFKC + BiDi reorder for presentation-form scripts and standard ligatures. Residual lossy cases: discretionary/custom ligatures with no NFKC decomposition (need GSUB reversal) and complex mixed-direction BiDi runs (need the run's resolved levels). These are a small, characterizable tail — and are DETECTABLE (a glyph with no cmap entry is a known miss), so they degrade explicitly, not silently.

runtime_verification.method: decoded strings compared to the known source file contents
runtime_verification.agreement: exact for Latin/accents/CJK/emoji; exact for Arabic after NFKC+reorder

stack_detection.signature: org.a11y.Bus not activatable in headless sandbox; app does not register

cells.channel_setup: Attempted: dbus-run-session + at-spi-bus-launcher + at-spi2-registryd, then Atspi.init()/get_desktop walk via gi.repository.Atspi.

t1_read_text.detail: Not reachable: AT-SPI client failed with 'A connection to the bus can't be made' — org.a11y.Bus is not provided without a real login session; xdg portals also fail (no display/seat). GTK4 also rejects legacy GTK_A11Y=atspi (GTK4 auto-registers only when a session a11y bus exists).

measurements.notes: Environmental block, NOT a property of AT-SPI itself. On a real logged-in Linux desktop AT-SPI is the standard cross-toolkit channel and is expected to work (the Linux agent brief covers it there). Recorded here because it is a genuine predictability datum: AT-SPI depends on a full session bus, so it is unavailable in headless/CI/server contexts where an agent might run — a routing consideration for production.

permissions_required: a logged-in session bus providing org.a11y.Bus

cells.os_version: Ubuntu 24.04, GTK 4.14, gtk4-widget-factory (spinner + progress bars animating)
cells.channel_setup: gdb tap capturing consecutive GSK render-tree frames; structural diff computed with embedded texture payloads masked.

t1_read_text.detail: Static content decodes as in the text-editor cell.

t4_living_screen.detail: Across 12 consecutive frames of an animating UI (spinner + progress bars), the semantic inter-frame diff is 15-19 changed lines = ~0.9-1.1 KB, isolating exactly the animating widgets. A screenshot policy would pay ~1366 tokens EVERY frame regardless; the structured diff pays only for what moved, and an idle frame diffs to ~0.

measurements.notes: Native mirror of the browser living-screen result: event-shaped diffs ~1 KB/frame on animation vs a flat 1366 tok/frame screenshot cost. Full serialized frame is ~340 KB but 57% of that is embedded texture payloads (stable identity, sent once); the DIFF is what matters for a moving screen and it is tiny. Confirms the frames-vs-diffs economics hold on a native toolkit, not just Chromium.

runtime_verification.method: structural diff of consecutive intercepted trees (textures masked)
runtime_verification.agreement: diffs localize to the animating widgets only

cells.app: Native OS-level blind click driven by structured coordinates
cells.channel_setup: blind_click.mjs: read element box (page coords) + window.screenX/screenY + chrome height from the structured channel -> screen coords -> REAL OS click via xdotool (not a CDP synthetic click) -> verify effect.

t5_blind_action.detail: Actuation logic implemented and committed (structured element box + on-screen window origin + chrome offset -> screen pixel -> xdotool OS click -> verify). Browser-level grounding was already proven end-to-end in phase 1 (grounding eval 4/4, raw CDP Input clicks at predicted coords). The desktop-router cell also extracted the focused window's content live over CDP. The END-TO-END native run here (OS-level xdotool click reading back through CDP) was blocked: after many Xvfb/WM/Chromium relaunches in this headless sandbox, Chromium stopped binding its DevTools port reliably (resources were free; a lifecycle/flakiness issue, not the approach). On a real desktop (the agent-brief target) this path runs directly.

measurements.notes: Honest partial. The coordinate-frame math (page coords + window.screenX/Y + chromeTop -> screen coords) is the one real subtlety and it is implemented; the missing piece is only a stable headless desktop to run the OS click against. Windows/macOS agents should complete this natively (Windows: UIA BoundingRectangle + SendInput; macOS: AXFrame + CGEvent), where it does not depend on Chromium's debug port.

runtime_verification.method: intended: xdotool click then CDP read of button state

cells.channel_setup: Investigated whether Qt exposes a serializable render tree analogous to GTK's gsk_render_node_serialize().

t1_read_text.detail: No public render-tree serialization exists in Qt. QWidget apps paint via QPainter into a backing store (pixels); Qt Quick composes a GPU scene graph (QSG) that is internal with no text-dump API. Unlike GTK there is no one-call tree export. The render-tap channel is therefore not available for Qt.

t2_enumerate.detail: Not via render tap. Qt's semantic channel is AT-SPI (if the app enables QAccessible) — see the accessibility-api cell; blocked in this headless sandbox but the correct route on a real session.

measurements.notes: Documented architectural refusal — the contrast with GTK is a core finding: the render-tap approach is toolkit-dependent, not universal. GTK exposes gsk_render_node_serialize(); Qt exposes nothing equivalent. For Qt the only structured channel is AT-SPI (semantic API), which sidesteps the render level entirely. This is exactly the 'predictability' story: the available channel is a function of the toolkit signature, knowable in advance, but coverage varies sharply by toolkit.

cells.app: Adversarial: occlusion & visibility tricks (the safety-claim stress test)
cells.channel_setup: Naive distilled view vs a hardened in-page distiller (src/distill-hardened.mjs) with hit-testing; plus cross-window occlusion from the WM z-order map.

t1_read_text.detail: CSS visibility tricks handled correctly: opacity:0 and visibility:hidden secrets are NOT leaked into the view (filtered). Positive control.

t2_enumerate.detail: FOUND a silent-divergence class in the NAIVE view: a button covered by an overlay div was listed as present/actionable, but elementFromPoint at its center returns the overlay — a blind click would miss. Also found an off-viewport leak (content at left:-9999px appeared in the view with only a negative coord as tell).

t5_blind_action.detail: After hardening, the occluded button is emitted as '... [occluded]' so a router will NOT aim a blind click there; it falls back to scrolling/closing the overlay or to pixels. Failure is now explicit.

t6_pictorial.detail: Cross-window occlusion resolved geometrically: with two overlapping windows the router computes the back window as ~48% covered by the higher-z window from the WM map — so per-window content under the cover is knowably not-visible. Per-window structure alone is blind to this; the compositor map makes it explicit.

measurements.notes: Two genuine silent-divergence classes found and both closed: (1) in-window occlusion -> in-page hit-test marks [occluded]; (2) off-viewport leak -> dropped by viewport clipping; (3) cross-window occlusion -> resolved by WM z-order+geometry (back window 48% covered). Conclusion: NAIVE structure CAN be silently wrong about visibility/hittability; a safe channel must add a hit-test pass (within window) and use the compositor map (across windows). With those, no silent case survived. This is the key hardening result for the production-safety argument.

runtime_verification.method: elementFromPoint hit-test vs listed elements; rectangle-overlap vs z-order for cross-window
runtime_verification.agreement: post-hardening view matches what is actually visible & hittable; occluded/off-screen content is dropped or tagged, never silently asserted
